column1: Fennel/s0|Did you discover it before morning?|Yes. I shut it, but took much longer to stop imagining what might have entered.|Do you check it each evening now?|Once, carefully. Rechecking all night would cost the sleep the latch was meant to protect.
Fennel/s1|Did your family grow fennel too?|Enough for the name to have been a deliberate joke.|Do you use what you grow?|In cooking. It is more useful in a meal than in another joke about my name.

Fennel/e0|What if the latch is damaged?|Then it needs repairing. Reminding myself I checked is useful only if it actually closes.|Have you been sleeping better?|Some nights. I try not to turn a bad night into another thing to worry over.

Fennel/e1|Is it difficult to grow here?|It needs care suited to the season. I cannot plant a name and expect the weather to oblige.|Do you enjoy tending it?|Yes. There is a definite task, and sometimes a definite result.

Fennel/w0|Have the patrols frightened you?|Their questions make an ordinary journey feel like something requiring an excuse.|Do you avoid the graveyard?|When I have no reason to go there, certainly.|What would make the road safer?|People dealing with real dangers instead of treating every traveller as one.

Fennel/w1|Will you walk farther now?|Perhaps gradually. I need not prove anything by frightening myself.|Why still latch the door?|It is a sensible household habit. I can keep it without assuming the worst about everyone outside.|What would a good evening be?|A little air, a conversation, and coming in because I am ready.

Bjorn/s0|Why did your father hide his hunger?|He did not want anyone to give up a share for him.|How do you avoid that happening now?|I set a portion aside for late arrivals instead of serving everything at once.

Bjorn/s1|What makes the broth good?|Time, suitable ingredients, and tasting it instead of relying on a grand description.|Do you change the recipe often?|According to what is available. I still want it to taste like supper, not an experiment on guests.

Bjorn/e0|Do you add more when someone arrives?|If there is time and enough ingredients. An empty space alone feeds nobody.|How do you plan the portions?|From who is expected, with a little margin when supplies allow.

Bjorn/e1|What if they truly have eaten?|They can decline. I offer without making them defend the answer.|Did you learn that from your father?|Yes. I remember how easily pride can sound like a full stomach.

Bjorn/w0|Can you keep feeding everyone?|Not alone. I do what I can with the ingredients available.|Why do people have less each winter?|Levies take what they might otherwise save for the lean months.|Do the collectors see hungry households?|They see the stores. They rarely wait to see what remains for supper.

Bjorn/w1|What can a neighbour bring?|Whatever they can spare that suits the meal. Help with the work counts too.|Will you still save a late portion?|Yes. A better year should not make us forget the people who arrive last.|What would a good winter look like?|Enough supplies, fewer worried faces, and a pot nobody must stretch beyond reason.

Cap/s0|Did you think sunlight suited every plant?|I knew better in theory and forgot to consider what this moss needed.|How did you know it was recovering?|Its color and growth improved after I restored the cooler, shaded conditions.

Cap/s1|Can a growing bed fail in winter?|Yes. That is why I keep other stores too rather than relying on one source.|What care does it need?|Conditions suited to what grows there, checked before there is an obvious problem.

Cap/e0|Could you shade it another way?|Yes. I choose whatever protects the bed without damaging it.|Do you prefer sitting near it?|I like seeing how it changes, provided my comfort does not ruin its shade.

Cap/e1|How often do you check the bed?|As conditions require. Warm or dry weather means paying closer attention.|Would dried stores be easier?|In some ways. A mix gives us fewer reasons to fear one failure.

Cap/w0|Did you explain it was a nursery?|Yes. They had decided its purpose before asking anyone who tended it.|Why did they want it cleared?|They saw an inconvenient patch of ground rather than something feeding a community.|Could you move it safely?|Not simply because somebody ordered it. Living beds have requirements.

Cap/w1|What does the nursery need now?|Care and time after the disturbance, not another set of boots measuring it.|Would you show visitors around?|Careful visitors, yes. Understanding begins with seeing what actually grows here.|Are you worried they will claim it again?|I would rather establish that our work and home are not empty land awaiting a claim.

Ilsa/s0|Was there no other food that spring?|Very little. Hunger made the immediate meal seem like the only decision.|Did the beds recover eventually?|With care and restraint. The shortage lasted longer because we had taken the new growth.
Ilsa/s1|Why use grass loops?|They make the protected shoots easy to recognise without pulling them up.|What if someone forgets?|We explain again. Punishment does not make an eaten shoot grow back.

Ilsa/e0|Do they choose which shoots to mark?|With guidance. They are learning what needs leaving to grow.|Do the loops harm the shoots?|They must be loose and checked. A marker should not cause the harm it is meant to prevent.

Ilsa/e1|What if people are hungry today?|We look for another way to share what is available. The future cannot be the only concern either.|Does planning make a shortage less frightening?|It makes the choices clearer. I would still prefer enough food for both months.

Ilsa/w0|Do the collectors understand the beds?|They count what could be taken now. They do not wait for the next season's shortage.|Have you tried explaining the young growth?|Yes. It is easier when someone wants to understand rather than justify a demand.|What does taking too much cause?|Less mature growth later, when people will still need to eat.

Ilsa/w1|How long will recovery take?|Several growing cycles, depending on the bed. I will not promise an exact harvest now.|Will the grass loops stay?|Yes. Good harvesting habits remain useful after the levy ends.|Could you have a feast later?|When there is genuinely enough to spare. A celebration should not eat the next season.

Meriel/s0|Had you hurt yourself?|No, fortunately. Sela made sure before we dealt with the broken glass.|Were you afraid of losing the job?|Very. Her first concern helped me admit what had happened honestly.

Meriel/s1|What if they know very little about the recipient?|I ask what the gift will be used for, rather than inventing a taste.|Do you ever suggest a simpler gift?|Often. Expensive and suitable are different questions.

Meriel/e0|How do you help them choose?|Ask about weight, use and what they enjoy looking at.|What if they leave without buying?|They should not buy the wrong thing merely to end an awkward conversation.

Meriel/e1|Do you point out imperfections?|Yes. A customer should know what they are carrying away.|Does different light change the color?|It can change how the glass appears. Seeing it clearly helps avoid disappointment.

Meriel/w0|What kind of complaint do they make?|Demands for special terms, presented as though questioning them insults the crown.|Can Sela support you?|She can, but neither of us should need courage to discuss a cup honestly.|Do ordinary buyers behave better?|Most understand a purchase involves two people agreeing.

Meriel/w1|Will royal customers pay the same way?|I want clear terms for everyone, without a title replacing payment.|Why ask about carrying it home?|Beautiful glass still has to survive the journey.|What is the best part of the change?|Being able to explain the work plainly without guessing which fact will offend a uniform.

Elin/s0|Did you still replace the chipped cup?|That remains the necessary purchase. I am trying to keep the two decisions separate.|Why did the flower catch your eye?|The colors looked different as the light moved. I kept stopping to look again.

Elin/s1|Would the flower fit your window?|I would check before buying it. Admiring it does not widen the frame.|Do you enjoy breakfast there already?|Yes. The flower would add something, not rescue a room I dislike.

Elin/e0|Is the table difficult to move?|Enough that I do not chase every inch of sunlight.|Would sitting on the other side help?|Sometimes. I am gradually discovering cheaper solutions than rearranging the room.

Elin/e1|Have you bought the flower yet?|Not yet. I am deciding what pleasure it would bring at home, as well as its price.|Can something lovely also be practical?|Certainly. I simply no longer think practicality requires plainness.

Elin/w0|Has the price risen too?|The levy mainly leaves me less to spend. The flower is still a choice I keep postponing.|Would you buy it before necessities?|No. That is why it remains an errand for another day.|Why does this small purchase matter?|Because I would like wanting one pleasant thing to be an ordinary decision.

Elin/w1|Will you buy it soon?|If the household money allows. I can consider it without another levy overtaking the plan.|Where would you put it?|In the morning light at home, after checking how to hang it safely.|Would you remember the change through a flower?|I would remember being able to choose something for my own pleasure.

Maelis/s0|How did you keep it from hurting the wing again?|Kept it sheltered and handled it as little as the care allowed.|Were you sorry when it left?|I was pleased it could manage without me. My fingers were pleased too.

Maelis/s1|Have you tried correcting the stories?|Repeatedly. An ordinary explanation competes poorly with a entertaining accusation.|What caused the sour milk?|Often poor storage. A household should check that before seeking a witch to blame.
Maelis/e0|Did it return afterwards?|Not to present thanks. It had a goose's life to get on with.|Would you help another one?|If I could. I would approach its beak with more respect.
Maelis/e1|What details are useful?|What happened, when, what changed, and what you directly observed.|Will you tell me if you don't know?|Yes. Pretending would make me a less useful person to ask.

Maelis/h|What dangers are real?|Uncertain footing and the creatures of the marsh, among others. Watch where you travel.|Why do people call living here sinister?|Distance and unfamiliar work leave room for invention. Asking us would be less entertaining.

Maelis/w0|Does he spread the rumours himself?|I cannot prove every source. I can see how convenient they are for his rule.|Why would fear of you help him?|It gives people a nearby figure to blame while official demands go unquestioned.|Can you stop that?|I can answer honestly. Other people must decide to ask honest questions.

Maelis/w1|What if someone repeats a lie unknowingly?|Correct the claim and explain why. Ignorance and deliberate deceit are different problems.|Will you be treated differently now?|Some people may reconsider. Others will need more than a change in ruler.|How should we check a frightening story?|Ask what was witnessed, what was inferred, and what evidence survives.

Archivist Elowen/s0|Did you tell the students about the demand?|They knew why keeping accurate copies mattered. I did not promise it was without risk.|What happened to the six names?|They remained in the preserved accounts. Removing them from one page could not erase every copy.

Archivist Elowen/s1|How do you help someone ask?|Begin with what they want to understand, without making ignorance embarrassing.|Do you still find questions you cannot answer?|Daily. Then the work is finding evidence or stating the limit honestly.

Archivist Elowen/e0|What do you say to that visitor?|That they may read, and that asking about an account is not agreeing with it.|Could they simply be looking for a seat?|Certainly. An observation is a reason to offer help, not to presume a secret.

Archivist Elowen/e1|Could the page simply be damaged?|Yes. A blank is something to investigate, not proof of censorship on its own.|How can you check a missing name?|Compare other copies and examine whether the gap was created deliberately.

Archivist Elowen/h|Was Halvard one of the seven?|Yes. His later histories should be read with his part in the betrayal in mind.|Why keep accounts calling them traitors?|They show what the crown wanted people to believe and how that account changed.

Archivist Elowen/w0|How do you preserve opposing accounts?|Keep accurate copies and record their sources, so comparison remains possible.|Do all opposing accounts deserve belief?|No. Opposition does not guarantee accuracy. They still require scrutiny.|Why is comparison such a threat to him?|It lets a reader notice claims that the approved version leaves unexplained.

Archivist Elowen/w1|Wouldn't destroying the lies be safer?|It would also destroy evidence of how people were misled.|How will pupils recognise the false claims?|By comparing them with evidence and learning the methods used to persuade.|Could our account become too comfortable?|Yes. That is why questions must remain welcome after a victory.

Mira/s0|Why give the letter more weight?|It describes the search directly. I still want other accounts to check its details.|Could both describe part of the event?|Yes. The report may count production while omitting the human cost.

Mira/s1|Could the entrance face both sunrise and a tavern?|It could. I need positions and directions before treating the descriptions as a contradiction.|Why draw several versions?|To show what is uncertain instead of silently choosing the one I prefer.

Mira/e0|Do you label the uncertain parts?|Yes. Light marks alone might not be obvious to the next reader.|What would make a detail certain enough?|Measurements or several reliable observations that agree.

Mira/e1|Can ordinary details help date a letter?|Sometimes, alongside other records. They can also explain the writer's circumstances.|Do you keep the whole letter?|Yes. Removing everything but the danger can distort what the writer wanted to say.

Mira/w0|Is a production delay a false description?|It can be factually narrow while concealing what matters most about the event.|How should the miners be recorded?|By name, with what happened to them, rather than only a lost output figure.|Can you recover the missing details?|Letters and family accounts may help, though some gaps must remain acknowledged.

Mira/w1|What will you ask the families?|What they know directly, what was reported to them, and what they want recorded.|What if their accounts disagree?|Preserve the disagreement and investigate it. Grief does not make memory identical.|Will they get to check your writing?|Where possible. They should be able to correct errors about their own lives.

Oren/s0|Do you think his chair ever answered?|I have no evidence it did. Remembering someone aloud is not itself a haunting.|Are the graveyard ghosts different?|There are real dangers there. I try to separate those from ordinary mourning.

Oren/s1|Do you scare easily at night?|After reading several frightening accounts, I become an enthusiastic interpreter of creaking wood.|Can you still work after sunset?|On other subjects. I have discovered I am allowed to choose the order.

Oren/e0|What do you read instead?|Something whose footsteps belong to living people with ordinary errands.|Does morning change the accounts?|It changes my response to them. The evidence should remain the same.

Oren/e1|What if a name is worn away?|Record what remains without inventing the missing letters.|Do you compare dates with other records?|When I can. A careful copy is the beginning, not the whole investigation.

Oren/w0|What do the royal accounts omit?|The people grieving and the work of caring for the dead afterwards.|Do you think battles should never be remembered?|They should be remembered fully, including the losses beyond the victory speech.|Why study those omissions?|Because leaving people unnamed makes their loss easier to dismiss.

Oren/w1|Can we celebrate without forgetting them?|Yes. Joy and grief can belong to the same day.|How will you recover their names?|Surviving records and families willing to speak, with uncertainty marked clearly.|What if a family wants privacy?|Then their grief is not ours to display merely because we want a complete account.

Tamsin/s0|Did the blue thread match?|Not at all. It made the repair easy to recognise.|Would you let someone else sit there?|If they needed it. Claiming a reading chair need not become governing a kingdom.

Tamsin/s1|Why is her brother missing?|That is the part I still need to decide. The reason should matter beyond opening an adventure.|Could the door lead somewhere ordinary?|Yes. An ordinary place can be surprising if she never expected to find it there.

Tamsin/e0|Is her brother in the kitchen?|That is what I am working toward. Finding him raises questions the doorway alone cannot answer.|Why is a kitchen surprising?|She expected something grand or dreadful. A familiar room in an impossible place unsettles her differently.

Tamsin/e1|Does the patch make it more comfortable?|The stuffing matters more than the color. I repaired both.|Did anyone help with the mending?|Someone checked my first stitches. I wanted it to last longer than my claim on the chair.

Tamsin/w0|How do you decide what to cross out?|Whether it serves the story I am writing. I do not pretend that revising fiction alters somebody's lived past.|Why does Halvard dislike their accounts?|They describe things his preferred version would rather omit.|Can stories challenge that?|They can prompt questions, but a historical claim still needs evidence.

Tamsin/w1|What do you want to write now?|Characters who ask difficult questions without the page itself becoming a risk.|Will your rulers all be villains?|No. I want them judged by what they do, not a rule that every crown must be praised.|Will you show people the pages?|When they are ready to read. Revision is still required, fortunately for my audience.

Master Iven/s0|Was the grandmother right about every name?|We checked what she knew against the map and other accounts.|Did the pupils enjoy the correction?|They enjoyed seeing that a teacher could learn during his own lesson.

Master Iven/s1|Can a map show where goods come from?|It helps trace routes. We also discuss the people and work those routes connect.|Does that change how pupils see strangers?|I hope it makes them curious about work already supporting their own lives.

Master Iven/e0|What if the pupil is mistaken?|We examine the reason together. Being allowed to question does not make every objection correct.|Do you admit your own mistakes openly?|I try. Otherwise my advice about evidence would be rather hollow.

Master Iven/e1|Should maps include every garden?|Not every map. Different maps serve different purposes.|How do you teach what a map omits?|Ask pupils to describe their own walk home, then compare it with a simple plan.

Master Iven/h|What did Forgewick send back?|Tools among other goods. Grain and fruit did not arrive without exchange and labour.|Could a blocked road hurt distant towns?|Yes. A missing delivery can affect people who never see the obstruction.

Master Iven/w0|What happens if a pupil questions the king?|I help them examine the claim carefully and consider where it is safe to discuss it.|Is praising him ever an acceptable answer?|If it answers the question and survives evidence. Compulsory praise does neither by itself.|What question do you ask most?|How do you know? Then I give them time to answer.

Master Iven/w1|Will the lessons change immediately?|Some discussions can become more open. Careful reading and arithmetic remain useful.|What if pupils disagree with you?|They should explain their reasons. I owe them the same courtesy.|Could a new ruler demand praise too?|Yes. A classroom should not become incurious whenever it likes the person in power.

Brin/s0|Could they have entered by different doors?|Certainly. I ask about their route before assuming one account is wrong.|Would you publish an uncertain sketch?|Only with its uncertainty clearly labelled.

Brin/s1|Why does the exact steepness matter?|It helps describe what a traveller must climb and whether two accounts refer to the same stair.|Would you go alone to measure it?|No. An interesting measurement is no reason to ignore the temples' dangers.

Brin/e0|Is a notebook scale enough?|For recording a drawing's proportions, not measuring a real stair by itself.|What equipment would you need?|Suitable measuring tools and a safe place to use them. Preparation comes before the number.

Brin/e1|What kind of evidence would settle it?|A reliable measured plan or observations I can place in the same orientation.|Could both doors exist?|Yes. I should test that possibility before choosing between them.

Brin/w0|What could studying the temples reveal?|Records of the riders and their work that do not begin with his reign.|Do you know that is why he objects?|It is my interpretation, not something he has admitted to me.|Are the ruins safe to study?|No. Their age and dangers require preparation, however interesting they are.

Brin/w1|What convenient stories worry you?|Claims we prefer because they make the past or our victory simpler.|How will you avoid inventing details?|Label uncertain sketches and compare accounts before drawing conclusions.|Would you include evidence against our assumptions?|I should. Otherwise I would only be decorating a story already decided.

Nell/s0|Where would you find the names?|Records and the people affected, checked as carefully as the royal account should have been.|Would names alone explain the decision?|No. They make it harder to discuss consequences as though nobody lived through them.
Nell/s1|Did Iven give you time?|Yes. Being hurried would only have made it harder.|Do other pupils feel the same?|Some. We do not all find the same questions equally easy to say aloud.

Nell/e0|Does saying it get easier?|A little. I do not mistake that for every place being safe to speak.|Does the class listen?|Usually. I appreciate them letting me finish rather than supplying the words.

Nell/e1|Can you always identify one household?|No. The question helps me look for actual people rather than leave the consequences abstract.|What do you ask them?|What changed in their daily lives and how they know why it changed.

Nell/w0|How did he acquire his authority?|Through the betrayal at Wingfall and the rule he established afterwards. I want the account examined, not merely repeated.|Why must you choose when to ask?|Because a sensible question can still carry consequences under his rule.|What does Iven mean by keeping it?|Do not discard the question simply because this is not a safe moment to voice it.

Nell/w1|What work should we examine?|Decisions about people's safety, resources and rights, and whether promises are kept.|Would a good ruler welcome criticism?|They should at least permit it and answer the substance.|Could praise still be deserved?|Of course. It should follow useful work, not be required before we may inspect it.

Sable/s0|Does a copied error prove deliberate deceit?|No. It shows a likely connection between texts. I still have to establish why the account changed.|Could both writers use an older source?|Yes. Comparing dates and other shared details helps trace the relationship.

Sable/s1|How do you begin checking?|Find the source of a claim and compare independent accounts where possible.|What if evidence remains incomplete?|Say so. Uncertainty is more honest than forcing a conclusion.
Sable/e0|Could the same mistake happen twice?|Yes. One shared misspelling is a clue, not a whole case.|What else would you compare?|Unusual wording, order of details and dates, alongside the error.

Sable/e1|Do you cross out the old conclusion?|I mark what changed and why, so I can follow my own reasoning later.|Does changing your mind feel embarrassing?|Sometimes. Leaving a known mistake uncorrected would bother me more.

Sable/w0|Why put the old copies away?|Without them, fewer readers can notice changes in the new account.|Are older accounts always truer?|No. Age is not proof; comparison is the point.|Can the school keep both?|We try. Preserving the comparison matters even when it is inconvenient.

Sable/w1|How do you show what changed?|Compare the passages directly and note their dates and sources.|What if a change was a correction?|Then the evidence should support it. Not every revision is dishonest.|Will future readers understand our notes?|If we explain our methods as carefully as our conclusions.
